name: param-uq-03-growth-stratified
title: Growth-stratified sensitivity — how does parameter influence vary across the cell cycle?
claim:
(planned) Parameter influence on growth/mass is stage-dependent across the
cell cycle, with elongation mattering most mid-cycle during peak biosynthesis.
question:
Does the sensitivity of growth/mass to the elongation knobs change across
cell-cycle progress θ (birth→division)? (RFC006 strategy 4.)
hypothesis:
Parameter influence is stage-dependent: elongation knobs (especially
basal_elongation_rate) matter most mid-cycle during peak biosynthetic activity,
and less so early (small cell, limited ribosome pool) and late (resources
committed to division).

report.title: param-uq-03-growth-stratified — cell-cycle-stratified Sobol sensitivity
report.objective:
Determine whether the elongation-rate dominance found in param-uq-01
(instantaneous_growth_rate, short window) and param-uq-02 (multi-observable,
360 steps) is uniform across the cell cycle or concentrated in specific
phases. Per-stage Sobol indices would reveal whether sensitivity is
episodic, guiding targeted intervention strategies.
report.setup:
Approach (RFC006 strategy 4):
- Run multi-generation simulations through ≥1 cell division (each ~2760 steps).
- Compute cell-cycle progress: θ = [log m(t) − log m_birth] / [log m_div − log m_birth],
  binned into 10 equal stages from birth (θ=0) to division (θ=1).
- For each stage bin, compute per-stage Sobol indices from the 3 effective
  elongation knobs (same as param-uq-01/02).

Infrastructure requirements:
(a) Multi-generation runs that record birth/division events — significantly
    slower than the 120–360-step windows used so far (~2760 steps per generation).
(b) Re-adding the growth-stratified aggregation strategy to pbg-uq (this was
    intentionally dropped from the thin core to keep the package minimal).

Parameters: same 3 effective knobs (basal_elongation_rate, kS,
chrom.basal_elongation_rate) with the same bounds as param-uq-01.
report.result: RESULTS PENDING — study not yet run.

assumptions.text:
The cell-cycle progress metric θ = [log m(t) − log m_birth] / [log m_div − log m_birth]
captures biologically meaningful stages. Division timing must be reliably
detected from the mass trajectory.

The 3 effective knobs from the 120-step screen remain the right parameter
set for cell-cycle-stratified analysis. No new knobs are expected to appear
at specific cell-cycle stages.

tests.name: per-stage-sensitivity-profile
tests.question:
Does basal_elongation_rate show significantly different Sobol indices across
cell-cycle stages (i.e., is sensitivity non-uniform across θ)?

measure.detail:
PLANNED metric — per-stage total-order Sobol for basal_elongation_rate across
10 θ bins (birth→division); pass if the across-stage range (max − min) exceeds
0.1, indicating stage-dependent influence. Not yet computed (study planned).

tests.cites_note: Stage-dependence detection threshold is methodological; not literature-derived.

study_card.goal:
(planned) Determine whether the elongation-rate dominance found in param-uq-01/02
is uniform across the cell cycle or concentrated in specific phases, via per-stage
(θ-binned, birth→division) Sobol indices over multi-generation runs.
study_card.why_before_next:
Per-stage sensitivity reveals whether parameter influence is episodic, which would
guide targeted intervention timing — the natural next resolution after the
window-dependence discovery in param-uq-02.

biological_summary:
(planned) Biosynthetic demand varies across the cell cycle, so elongation-rate
influence may be stage-dependent: hypothesized strongest mid-cycle during peak
biosynthesis, weaker early (small cell, limited ribosome pool) and late (resources
committed to division). This study would test that hypothesis with cell-cycle-resolved Sobol.

literature_anchors.expectation:
Cell-cycle progress can be tracked as a log-mass fraction between birth and
division; ergodic / age-structured analyses relate single-cell cycle position to
population statistics.
literature_anchors.model_observable: θ from listeners.mass over a multi-generation trajectory
literature_anchors.source: Kuritz et al. 2017 (cell-cycle analysis via ergodic principles)
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Planned — θ metric defined but not yet computed in v2ecoli.

model_change.notes:
(planned) No biological model change. Infrastructure work only: multi-generation
runs that record birth/division events, plus a growth-stratified aggregation
strategy re-added to pbg-uq.

implementation_requirements.title: Multi-generation runs recording birth/division events
implementation_requirements.description:
Run ≥1 division per sample (~2760 steps/gen) and emit birth/division markers so θ
can be computed per cell cycle. Substantially slower than the 120–360-step windows used so far.

implementation_requirements.title: Re-add growth-stratified aggregation strategy to pbg-uq
implementation_requirements.description:
Implement the RFC006 strategy-4 per-θ-bin Sobol aggregation in pbg-uq (dropped
from the thin core). Required before this study can run.
